BILL NUMBER:  S4334

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the civil rights law, in relation to sealing certain
court papers upon applications for a change of name


 PURPOSE :

To Protect the Contact and Identifying information of applicants for
unpublished identity changes during the pendency of their name change
proceeding.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

The bill amends the Civil Rights law section 64-a, to exempt the
publication of a name change for victims of domestic violence,
stalking, or other crimes to ensure their personal safety.

 EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW WHICH THIS BILL WOULD ALTER :

Add a new subsection to Civil Rights Law Section 64-a.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 1994, the Civil Rights Law section 64-a was amended to respond to
the safety and confidentiality needs of name change applicants for
whom publication would jeopardize their personal safety, such as
victims of domestic violence, stalking, or other crimes. Under this
law, court orders granting exemption from publication requirements and
sealing the case record has long provided significant protection to
those victims forced to change their identities as an extreme safety
planning measure.

Although applicants can obtain a court order sealing their pleadings
and other records associated with their name would jeopardize the
applicants personal safety, the statute does not currently provide for
similar temporary relief that authorizes the sealing and
non-disclosure of court records and identifying information while the
case is pending. Failure to safeguard the information contained in
these extremely sensitive records may seriously compromise the safety
of sealed name change applicants. For example, if a pending case is
not sealed, an applicant's information can be easily found by the
offender, a person acting on the offender's behalf, or anyone
accessing the Unified Court System's public E-Courts site simply by
conducting a search by county, party name, judge, attorney of record,
or anyone index number in the webCiviSupreme databases. If the
information is posted on this website or otherwise publicly available
the very person from who the victim is seeking anonymity can obtain
potentially dangerous information related to the case name, case type,
case status and dates for future Court appearances. As a result,
unless the name change applicant or judge is specifically aware of
these hidden challenges, the applicant's safety can be inadvertently
jeopardized during this critical and, potentially, lengthy time period
before a finding. This bill requires a Court to order the sealing and
safeguarding of an applicant's identifying information, pleadings and
other court records after the case is commenced and until a final
decision is rendered.

Recognizing the safety risks that disclosure of sensitive contact
information can pose to domestic violence and child abuse survivors
with pending litigation, the legislature has already enacted
provisions allowing a party to obtain address confidentiality in
various civil proceedings including Family Court (Family Court Act
Section 154-b(2) (a); Family Court Act Section 580-312); Supreme Court
(Domestic Relations Law Section 254) Custody and dissolution
proceedings, as well as in all other civil proceedings (CPLR Section
2103-a) and to have this information temporarily safeguarded and
sealed prior to a formal finding by the Court. This bill falls within
this increasing category of confidentiality-related protections for
litigants.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2008, A.10243 (Scarborough) passed assembly

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides that certain court papers submitted on application for a name change shall be sealed.
